verdict.T1_last_third_party: The order machinery works. Only the in-order model solves it (0.975). The unordered model scores the same as no order at all (about 0.70), so it cannot see the order of what other characters did.

why.h: The two versions score the same
why.b: Ordered and unordered differ by 0.002 PR-AUC within films and 0.003 across films, and both 95% intervals include zero. Ordering the events adds no measurable information.

why.h: Most of the order falls inside a single scene
why.b: About two thirds of neighbouring events from other characters come from the same scene, where their sequence says little about the story. The order that spans scenes is a smaller signal.

why.h: Both versions already see the most recent events
why.b: Each model reads the latest 48 events involving other characters, so recency is built into both versions. Putting those events in order adds little beyond that.

why.h: 51 films is a modest amount of data
why.b: The ordered model has extra position information to learn from about 19,000 training decisions. A larger corpus could reveal order effects that this one cannot.

why.h: Other characters' events add little, so their order cannot add much
why.b: The pair's own history adds +0.099 PR-AUC over chance and their relationship adds +0.016. Other characters' events add +0.005 on top. Order can only refine information that is already small.
